body:
## Result and scope

Complete negative answer to the **literal exact-minimizer formulation** of problem **30004064 / OWR-16766-003**, in one substantive attempt.

For noiseless data y=As with s in [-1,1]^N, expanding the objective gives F(mu)-F(0) >= ||mu||^2/2. Hence its unique optimizer is zero. A full-row-rank 3-by-3 row/column tomography instance has exactly two binary solutions and five common pixels, but the stated exact sign-recovery rule returns zero.

**The cited paper already acknowledges the scalar obstruction. No novelty or historical-priority claim is made.** Finite-iterate algorithms, smoothing limits, and methods using an additional primal/subgradient variable are not settled by this result.

## Review and verification

- Complete independent adversarial audit: PASS for the literal exact-minimizer scope, with no required revisions.
- Frozen proof, source reconciliation, attempt log, exact checks, complete audit, and integrity manifests are preserved.
- Original exact checks: 1,044 binary images; 1,458 objective identities; 729 projected-objective cases; eight scalar approximation identities.
- Independent audit: 528 binary images, 1,400 box-feasible objective identities, and larger tomography-family/rank checks.
- Dependency-free verification uses exact integers and rational arithmetic. Finite checks supplement the universal proof.
- Queue edit is restricted to this problem's Status, Turns, and previously blank Findings cells: claimed_solved, 1/5.

See [publication status and package](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/dot/math-30004064-exact-dual-recovery/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004064/PUBLICATION_STATUS.md).

This is a draft for review. No merge, release, source-paper copies, copied implementation code, or external outreach is included.
title: 30004064: exact-dual zero-minimizer obstruction in binary tomography
